_readme: This file seeds the VASP / Entity Intelligence Database (app.db.models.KnownEntity).
It ships with only a handful of UNAMBIGUOUS, publicly-documented addresses
(null/burn addresses) so the app has something to demo against out of the box.
Claude did not fabricate exchange/mixer/VASP address attributions here on purpose:
an investigation tool is exactly the wrong place for a guessed address-to-entity
mapping, since 'confidence: confirmed' on a wrong address can misdirect a real
case. Populate this list for real from licensed/verifiable sources instead:
- Your own confirmed case attributions (subpoena returns, exchange KYC responses)
- CryptoScamDB exports (scam-tagged addresses): https://cryptoscamdb.org
- Chainabuse exports (community-reported malicious addresses): https://chainabuse.com
- A licensed blockchain-intelligence feed (Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Elliptic), if
your unit already subscribes to one -- their labels are exactly what the
'source' / 'source_date' / 'confidence' fields below are designed to record.
- Manually, as your own investigations confirm entities -- every confirmed VASP
candidate from a closed case should get added back into this table.
Load this file with:  python -m app.db.seed_entities
Schema per entry:
name          human-readable entity name
entity_type   vasp | exchange | dex | mixer | bridge | custodian | scam | ransomware
chain         ethereum | polygon | bitcoin | tron
address       lowercase hex (EVM) or base58/bech32 (Bitcoin)
source        where this attribution came from
source_date   ISO date the attribution was recorded/verified
evidence      short note on how this was attributed
confidence    observed | inferred | attributed | confirmed  (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)

entities.name: Null address (burn / contract-creation sentinel)
entities.evidence: Reserved zero address; used for token burns and as the 'from' address of contract-creation traces. Any funds sent here are unrecoverable.

entities.name: Common EIP burn address (...dEaD)
entities.evidence: Widely-used vanity burn address across many ERC-20 token contracts.
